data.angle: Compare the nine AI SEO agencies in Searchbloom’s 2026 ranking by strengths, reported results, scores and published costs, noting that the publisher ranks itself first.

ranked_sections.reason: Contains all nine core agency profiles, with distinct capabilities, scorecards, reported client results, pricing and limitations; representative examples anchor the comparison.
Provides the complete ranking and directly compares all nine agencies’ scores, best-fit situations and published fees.
Makes substantive comparisons for local businesses, B2B, AI Overviews, ChatGPT and technically complex sites, explaining why different agencies fit different needs.
Adds meaningful commercial differences, including published starting fees, minimums and contract terms across the nine agencies.
Establishes the leading agencies and explicitly attributes the ranking to Searchbloom, which places itself first, while giving the verification date.
Explains the five equally weighted scoring criteria and identifies case-study figures as agency-reported, providing necessary context for interpreting scores and results.
Compares disclosure completeness and distinguishes dated AI results from SEO-only evidence, but largely overlaps the profiles and pricing tables.
Uses named agencies’ reported timelines to contextualize results, though those examples are already available in the core profiles.
Recaps platform-specific results, prices and Searchbloom’s self-ranking rationale, but substantially duplicates the selected comparison material.
Defines AEO and GEO and explains technical, content and third-party authority work, useful background rather than the agency comparison itself.
Details prompt tracking and visibility metrics, but a measurement tutorial is secondary to comparing the ranked agencies.
Clarifies agency responsibilities, internal brand work and red flags, supporting service expectations without adding much agency-specific comparison.
Offers a hiring checklist and questions to ask, but generic selection advice should not displace the ranked companies and their reported differences.
Adds author perspective, comparative concessions and an update log; the essential self-ranking disclosure is already retained in the opening.
Describes reported Google policy and feature changes in 2026, which are broader industry context rather than central evidence about the nine agencies.
